Alexander Hamilton was a founding father of the United States and its first secretary of the treasury, from 1789 to 1795. He was born in Charlestown on Nevis in the Caribbean, an orphan whose talent won him passage to New York.

He served as an aide to George Washington in the Revolutionary War. With James Madison and John Jay he wrote the Federalist Papers to win support for the Constitution.

At the treasury he had the federal government take over the states' war debts, founded the First Bank of the United States and pushed for manufacturing, building the credit of the new nation. His fights with Thomas Jefferson gave rise to the first political parties. He was killed in a duel by Vice President Aaron Burr in 1804.
